RD001.name: unpinned-dependency
RD001.fix: Pin exact versions (e.g. "1.2.3"), commit a lockfile, and let Dependabot/Renovate propose upgrades through reviewed pull requests.

RD002.name: missing-lockfile
RD002.fix: Commit package-lock.json / yarn.lock / pnpm-lock.yaml and install with `npm ci`. For Python use `pip-compile --generate-hashes` + `pip install --require-hashes`, or uv/poetry lock files.

RD003.name: known-compromised-package
RD003.fix: Remove or upgrade immediately, rotate every secret reachable from machines or CI that installed it, and review lockfile history for when it entered.

RD004.name: hardcoded-secret
RD004.fix: Remove it from source, revoke/rotate the credential now (assume it leaked, git history included), and load it from an environment variable or a secret manager. Add a secret-scanning pre-commit hook.

RD005.name: end-of-life-runtime
RD005.fix: Upgrade to a supported release. If you cannot yet, isolate the service, add virtual patching (WAF rules) and set a dated retirement plan.

RD006.name: ai-agent-config-risk
RD006.fix: Apply least privilege: allow only specific commands, keep human approval for sensitive actions, pin MCP server versions, and reference secrets as ${ENV_VAR} instead of literals.

RD007.name: unpinned-github-action
RD007.fix: Pin third-party actions to a full 40-character commit SHA (keep a `# v4.1.0` comment) and let Dependabot update them.

RD009.name: github-actions-workflow-risk
RD009.fix: Run untrusted pull-request code only without secrets, put untrusted values in env: and quote them in the script, give the workflow the least permissions it needs (permissions: contents: read), and never pipe a download into a shell.
